headline: Pershing Square sold Netflix at a loss in 2022. In Q2 2026 it was back.
dek: Pershing Square’s Q2 2026 13F reported $19.47B across 14 issuers. Five positions were new. Netflix was one of them, at 4.80% of the reported value.
cardSummary: Five new positions, including Netflix. Uber, Brookfield and Microsoft still carried the most weight.

sections.heading: Predictable businesses, concentrated positions
paragraphs: Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square looks for businesses with durable competitive advantages, understandable earnings and strong free cash flow. Its approach is concentrated and long-term.
The Q2 2026 report listed 15 rows for 14 issuers. Howard Hughes appears in two rows, which we combine into one position.

sections.heading: Five new names, one exit
paragraphs: [Visa](company:visa) (5.76%), [Mastercard](company:mastercard) (5.61%), [S&P Global](company:sp-global) (5.43%), [Netflix](company:netflix) (4.80%) and [Pershing Square USA](company:pershing-square-usa) (0.77%) were not in the Q1 2026 reports. Together they were 22.36% of the reported value.
[Alphabet](company:alphabet) left. The Q1 2026 reports listed 344,102 Alphabet shares worth $98.73M. The Q2 report listed none.

sections.heading: The Netflix return
paragraphs: Pershing Square sold its Netflix stake in 2022 after a loss reported at about $400 million. At June 30, 2026 it held 13,081,465 Netflix shares worth $934.02M, or 4.80% of the reported value. That made Netflix the 11th-largest position, not one of the biggest bets.

sections.heading: Where the weight sat
paragraphs: [Uber](company:uber), [Brookfield](company:brookfield) and [Microsoft](company:microsoft) together were 37.20% of the reported value.

Pershing added shares of Uber (+14.58%), Microsoft (+9.77%), [Restaurant Brands](company:restaurant-brands-international) (+14.02%) and [Meta](company:meta) (+20.11%). It reduced [Amazon](company:amazon) shares by 25.22%, Brookfield by 3.71% and [Hertz](company:hertz) by 1.64%. [Howard Hughes](company:howard-hughes) and [Seaport Entertainment](company:seaport-entertainment) share counts did not change.

sections.heading: Value change is not new money
paragraphs: The reported 13F value rose from $14.28B at the end of Q1 2026 to $19.47B at the end of Q2. That change mixes price moves with buying and selling. It does not measure money flowing into the fund.

cover.headline: Ackman gives Netflix another shot
cover.body: Pershing Square’s biggest Q2 holdings, and the Netflix comeback.

intro.title: Predictable businesses. Concentrated positions.
intro.body: Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square looks for businesses with durable competitive advantages, understandable earnings and strong free cash flow. The 2026 return to Netflix adds a reversal: a company Ackman sold at a large loss in 2022 was back in the portfolio.

outro.title: Netflix was the comeback. Not the biggest bet.
outro.body: Uber, Brookfield and Microsoft together accounted for 37.20% of the reported value. Netflix was 4.80%.

holdingNotes.visa: Visa operates a global payments network connecting financial institutions, merchants and consumers. Its revenue is tied to payment activity and related services, giving Pershing exposure to digital commerce without directly operating the merchants themselves.
holdingNotes.meta: Meta operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger. Advertising generates most of its revenue, tying its economics to audience engagement and advertiser demand rather than directly to the sale of AI models.
holdingNotes.restaurant-brands-international: Restaurant Brands owns Burger King, Tim Hortons, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs. Its largely franchised system earns royalties and related fees across global restaurant networks.
holdingNotes.howard-hughes: Howard Hughes combines master-planned communities and commercial real estate with specialty insurer Vantage, acquired in June 2026. The listed common stock is not Pershing’s entire economic relationship with the company.
holdingNotes.amazon: Amazon operates a retail marketplace, logistics network, advertising business and AWS. Those businesses give it several revenue engines, spanning repeat consumer purchases, third-party sellers and enterprise demand for cloud computing.
holdingNotes.microsoft: Microsoft sells enterprise software and cloud services, including Microsoft 365 and Azure. Subscriptions and usage-based cloud revenue connect the business to customers’ daily workflows, while AI adds another layer of demand and investment.
holdingNotes.brookfield: Brookfield combines asset management, insurance-based wealth solutions and ownership of infrastructure, renewable power and real estate. It gives Pershing exposure to long-duration assets and capital allocation across several businesses.
holdingNotes.uber: Uber connects customers with drivers, couriers and merchants through its mobility and delivery platforms. It earns revenue from repeated transactions across a shared network rather than from owning a large fleet of vehicles.
holdingNotes.netflix: Netflix earns subscription and advertising revenue from its global streaming service. Pershing’s renewed position is a different assessment from its 2022 exit.
